title: Someone Else's Socket
description: The real-time tracking WebSocket takes its access token as a query parameter, since browsers can't attach an Authorization header to a WS upgrade. Confirm a missing or invalid token is still rejected there just as strictly as it would be on a normal REST call.
successCondition: Open a WebSocket connection to /api/tracking/ws with no token query parameter at all — the server closes it with close code 4001. A second connection attempt to /api/tracking/ws?token=not-a-real-token (a syntactically invalid/garbage token) also closes with code 4001. A third connection using a genuine, freshly obtained accessToken succeeds and receives a { "type": "connected" } message before anything else.
hints: Most WebSocket client libraries expose the close event's code property directly — capture it rather than just checking that the connection ended.
Obtain a real access token via POST /api/auth/login for the success case, and pass it as ?token=<accessToken> in the WS URL exactly as documented in docs/api/tracking.md.
